memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Do not offer the blood of a sacrifice to me along with anything containing yeast. The fat of my festival offerings must not be kept until morning. Bring the best of the firstfruits of your soil to the house of the Lord your God. Do not cook a young goat in its mother's milk." - Exodus 23:18-19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
These instructions may seem strange to us, but a common thread runs through them: God is worthy of care, reverence, and our very best. The offerings were not to be handled carelessly or left to spoil. The firstfruits brought to God were to be the best of the soil, not the shabby leftovers. Even in the details of worship, God taught His people that He deserves excellence, not carelessness.

The command to bring "the best of the firstfruits" gets to the heart of it. God is not honoured by half-hearted, leftover offerings. He gave His people everything, and He asks that what they bring back to Him reflect genuine gratitude and reverence. How we worship — with care or with carelessness — reveals how highly we regard the One we worship.

This searches our own worship today. Do we give God our best attention, our best effort, our best love — or the tired scraps of a distracted heart? God is not impressed by mere ritual, but He does delight in worship that flows from a heart that treasures Him and therefore offers Him its finest. And behind all these ancient offerings stands the perfect offering of Christ, who gave His very best — Himself, without blemish — for us (Heb 9:14). In grateful response to such a gift, how could we offer Him anything less than our best?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I give God my best, or the tired leftovers of a distracted heart?
How does the reverence God deserves shape the way I worship Him?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You gave Your very best for me in Christ. Forgive my careless, leftover worship, and help me offer You my finest attention, effort, and love in glad gratitude. Amen.
